$description: High Contrast Dark — the black-and-white twin of the main dark theme, and the dark member of the WCAG-AAA 'high-contrast' family. Fully monochrome by construction: every color resolves to the achromatic core.mono ramp, so no hue survives anywhere — not in status, not in diffs, not in the ANSI palette. State is carried by lightness (an alarm is the brightest thing on screen, a healthy reading the dimmest) on top of the glyphs and labels the consuming surfaces already draw; nothing in this theme depends on a viewer distinguishing red from green. It mirrors the main theme's *structure* (same surface stack, same emphasis ordering), not the retro family's, which is what it inherited before this remap. AAA gates against bg.primary (#000000), via validate.py's own contrast_ratio(): text.primary 21.00:1 (>=7), text.secondary 13.08:1 (>=7), text.muted 7.37:1 (>=4.5), accent.base 21.00:1 (>=4.5), accent.on 21.00:1 on accent.base (>=7).

primary.$description: Pure black; anchors every AAA gate below.

muted.$description: 7.37:1 vs bg.primary — the dimmest ramp step that still clears the AAA 4.5:1 floor with margin.

base.$description: White is the accent: in a monochrome theme, emphasis is maximum lightness. 21.00:1 vs bg.primary.

light.$description: The hover/secondary accent shade — a step down from white so a hover state is still felt without hue.

on.$description: Foreground for text/icons on accent.base fills (e.g. primary buttons). 21.00:1 on white.

accent-secondary.$description: The decorative secondary-accent group; monochrome here, sitting one emphasis tier below accent.* so surfaces that pair the two still read as two tiers.

status.$description: The monochrome emphasis ladder, brightest = most urgent: error (white) > warning > success (dim). Consuming surfaces carry the glyph and label that name the state; this only sets how loudly it is drawn.

default.$description: Twice the alpha the chromatic themes use for their hairline — on pure black a 0.12 composite all but disappears, and a high-contrast theme must keep its structure legible.

tint.$description: Every tint family composites the same pure white, because monochrome means the accent/accent-secondary/error/success/neutral washes differ only in strength, never in hue.

error-dialog.$description: The error dialog's halo goes white with the rest of the palette — it is the only glow in the theme, which is what marks the dialog as the error one.

diff.$description: Additions read bright, deletions read dim — the only distinction a monochrome diff can carry beyond the +/- gutter the renderer already draws.

ansi.$description: The 16 ANSI slots spread across the light half of the mono ramp: program output that colors itself still separates into distinct tones, it just separates by lightness instead of hue. The bright-* slots sit one to two steps above their normal twins, capped at pure white.

chart.$description: Plots follow the theme: black paper, white-at-10% grid, and a 6-slot categorical palette that separates by lightness. A monochrome categorical palette tops out around six legible steps on this canvas — a plot needing more series should carry markers or dashes, not more grays.

pane-bg.$description: 3D scene axis panes (Plotly scene.*axis.backgroundcolor): bg.secondary, one step off the plot canvas.

axis-line.$description: Axis and legend lines (Plotly *.linecolor, legend.bordercolor): border.default, white at 24% alpha.

theme.$description: No dedicated high-contrast highlight.js theme is vendored; reuses the dark family's asset name (contract-tested against src/osprey/interfaces/vendor_manifest.json). Syntax highlighting is therefore the one surface this theme does not make monochrome.
